title: BMA executor lifecycle types
description: Token bootstrap, registration, capabilities, heartbeat and drain.

ExecutorInfo.description: Executor identity reported at token bootstrap and registration.

labels.description: Contract 1.4.0, optional. Labels the executor reports about itself (at most 32, each 1-64 characters of a-z 0-9 . _ -), set by the machine's owner in the executor's local configuration (for example BMA_LABELS or the SDK Options.Labels). The platform accepts them as given and does not validate their meaning, and it adds its own os:<os> and arch:<arch> labels from os and arch. Labels only narrow a choice among machines the project is already authorized to use (environment placement selectors); no authorization or security decision depends on them. Omitted: no labels.

secret_env.description: The executor accepts transport.secret_env on stdio servers: resolved secret values it injects only into the server process environment, never persisting, logging or echoing them. Without it the server keeps secret: references in env, which the executor rejects.

DisplayCapability.description: v1.1 display object. v1 sent a boolean; the server accepts both.

desktop.description: The machine can host its own desktop for a desktop session (it carries bma-desktop-session, started through process.start). Absent means unknown (an executor that predates the field).

ProcessCapability.description: v1.1 process.* support. pty, file_transfer, package_install and git_credentials are additive: the harness only sends the matching process.start fields to an executor that set them, and fails the process explicitly otherwise.

ArtifactCapability.description: v1.1 artifact upload (POST /v1/environments/{environment_id}/artifacts; legacy alias POST /v1/executors/artifacts). Environment-scoped executors only.

TerminalCapability.description: v1.1 terminal.* support. Machine-scoped executors only.

WorkspaceCapability.description: workspace.backup support and the startup restore of a pending backup. Machine-scoped executors only.

FsCapability.description: Session file views mounted by the executor as FUSE file systems backed by bma-file (docs/adr/0021). Declared only after the executor probed that it can mount. Absent or fuse=false: the session files stay on the copy-and-scan protocol (session_files). views lists the views the executor can mount; the harness only mounts those. Machine-scoped executors only.

SessionFilesCapability.description: Executor-owned per-session file layout. The harness derives <root>/<agent_session_id>/uploads (read-only session inputs) and <root>/<agent_session_id>/outputs (deliverables) from it, with agent_session_id as sent in process.start metadata, and uses these real paths in prompts, tool descriptions, write rules and the session files manifest. Absent: the harness keeps /mnt/session/uploads and /mnt/session/outputs. Fixed at executor.register: executor.capabilities.update does not change it. Machine-scoped executors only.

root.description: Absolute, already-expanded, clean path on the executor host (no ~, no . or .. segments, no trailing /).

RemoteBrainCapability.description: Contract 1.4.0. The machine's owner allows a brain that runs on another machine to use this machine as its hands (platform tools routed here for a session whose brain machine is a different one). Set only by the executor's local configuration (bmad configuration or SDK Options.RemoteBrain); the platform reads it back and cannot switch it on through any API. Absent or enabled=false: off, which is also what an executor that predates 1.4.0 means. It applies to a BYO (tenant-owned) machine; a platform pool machine does not need it. It does not restrict a platform-hosted brain driving this machine (project authorization is enough there), and a brain and hands on one machine never need it.

Capabilities.description: Executor capability object. The server only sends a method to an executor that advertised its capability; otherwise the executor answers -32012 capability_unavailable.

display.description: v1 boolean or v1.1 DisplayCapability object.

ExecutorRegisterResult.description: executor.register result. protocol and limits are v1.1 only.

ExecutorTokenRefreshResult.description: executor.token.refresh result: the connection now closes with 4001 at expires_at.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 time of the new connection deadline.

ExecutorTokenRequest.description: Token request body for POST /v1/machines/{machine_id}/token (bearer: machine daemon token) and POST /v1/environments/{environment_id}/token (bearer: environment key); the legacy alias POST /v1/executors/token takes either bearer. The id in the path must equal the credential's machine or environment, otherwise 404; on the new paths environment_id may be empty or absent for a machine and, when sent for an environment, must equal the path id. An empty environment_id with a machine token requests a machine-scoped executor: its executor_id is exec_<machine_id>, stable across refreshes, and the JWT carries machine_id and daemon_token_id.

ExecutorTokenResponse.description: Token response of POST /v1/machines/{machine_id}/token, POST /v1/environments/{environment_id}/token and the legacy alias POST /v1/executors/token.

token.description: Short-lived executor JWT, sent only in the Authorization header of the channel upgrade.
